---
title: "Types"
---

## Column types

Every column has one type from the `Phibble\Type` enum. The print header shows
tibble's abbreviation for each type.

| Type | Values | Printed as |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Type::Float` | `float` | `<dbl>` |
| `Type::Int` | `int` | `<int>` |
| `Type::Bool` | `bool` | `<lgl>` |
| `Type::String` | `string` | `<chr>` |
| `Type::Factor` | level labels, stored as codes | `<fct>`, or `<ord>` when ordered |
| `Type::Date` | `DateTimeImmutable` at midnight UTC | `<date>` |
| `Type::DateTime` | `DateTimeImmutable` | `<dttm>` |
| `Type::List` | any PHP value, including data frames | `<list>` |

`null` is NA in every type. `$df->types()` returns the types by column name
and `$df->type('x')` returns one.

## Inference

phibble infers a column's type from its PHP values the way R's `c()` combines
values:

- Bools and ints combine to int, and ints and floats combine to float.
- Any string makes the column a string column, and the other values are
  converted to text.
- `DateTimeInterface` values make a datetime column.
- Arrays and other objects make a list-column.
- A column that is entirely NA is bool, R's logical type.

{{< include examples/_infer.md >}}

Text read from CSV files and databases is guessed differently. The
[input and output guide](io.qmd) describes that.

## Casts

`cast()` converts columns to other types. Conversions follow R's `as.*()`
functions. A value that cannot be converted becomes NA, and phibble raises one
`E_USER_WARNING` per column, as R does with "NAs introduced by coercion".

- Floats convert to int by truncating toward zero.
- `"TRUE"`, `"true"`, `"T"`, and `"True"` convert to true. `"yes"` and `"1"` do
  not.
- Floats convert to text with up to 15 significant digits, in fixed or
  scientific notation, whichever is shorter.

{{< include examples/_casts.md >}}

A factor converts to int or float as its 1-based level codes, as
`as.integer(factor)` does in R. Converting it to text gives its labels. Dates
convert to numbers as days since 1970-01-01, and datetimes as seconds since the
epoch.

## Factors

A factor column stores an ordered list of level labels and one code per row.
`asFactor()` sorts the unique values to make the levels unless levels are
given. Numbers sort numerically and text sorts in byte order. Values that are
not among explicit levels become NA.

`levels()` returns the labels. `storage('x')->codes()` returns the codes, which
are 0-based indexes into the levels. An ordered factor sorts by level position.

{{< include examples/_factors.md >}}

The forcats functions are `fct*` methods. Each returns a new data frame with the
column's levels changed.

| Method | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `fctRelevel($col, $levels, after: 0)` | Moves the given levels to the front, or after a position. |
| `fctLevels($col, $levels)` | Sets the full level order. |
| `fctRev($col)` | Reverses the level order. |
| `fctInorder($col)` | Orders levels by first appearance. |
| `fctInfreq($col)` | Orders levels by frequency, most common first. |
| `fctReorder($col, $by, $summary)` | Orders levels by a summary of another column, the median by default. |
| `fctRecode($col, ['new' => 'old'])` | Renames levels. |
| `fctCollapse($col, ['new' => ['a', 'b']])` | Merges levels. |
| `fctDrop($col)` | Removes levels that no row uses. |

{{< include examples/_forcats.md >}}

## Dates and datetimes

A date column holds `DateTimeImmutable` values at midnight UTC. A datetime
column holds `DateTimeImmutable` values with their time and time zone. CSV text
in ISO 8601 form is parsed as a date when it has no time, and as a datetime
otherwise. Text without an offset is read as UTC.

{{< include examples/_dates.md >}}

## List-columns

A list-column holds any PHP value in each row, such as arrays or other data frames.
`nest()` collapses columns into a list-column of data frames, one row per unique
combination of the remaining columns. `unnest()` expands it again.

{{< include examples/_list-columns.md >}}

## Model data

`toModelData()` returns columns in the form phit's model functions read.
Numbers, bools, and strings are plain lists. Dates and datetimes become days
and seconds since the epoch. A factor becomes an array with its levels, its
0-based codes, and whether it is ordered, so a model keeps the data frame's level
order, including unused levels. A list-column throws.

{{< include examples/_model-data.md >}}
